q: How does a nitric acid plant in the Vaal Triangle report N2O for CBAM?
title: Vaal nitric acid N2O for CBAM
short: Measure it. For nitric acid, a CBAM fertiliser good, N2O must be determined with a measurement-based method in the definitive period: analysers for N2O concentration and flow in the tail gas, converted to CO2e with the GWP set in the CBAM rules. Ammonia used is a precursor.
audience: Ammonia, nitric acid and fertiliser producers in the Vaal Triangle, including Sasolburg, selling to the EU

p: N2O from the oxidation of ammonia over platinum gauzes varies with gauze age, pressure and temperature. IPCC default factors range widely by plant type, so the CBAM monitoring rules require continuous measurement for N2O at each emission point.

ul: Measured N2O from tail gas, converted to CO2e.
Embedded emissions of ammonia consumed, from your own ammonia plant or the supplier.
Fuel burnt on site and electricity used, because fertiliser goods count indirect emissions.

p: South Africa's carbon tax applies to process emissions such as N2O. A tax effectively paid on the embedded emissions can be claimed as a reduction under Article 9, net of allowances and offsets that lowered the tax bill, with independent certification.
